title: TileLang: A Composable Tiled Programming Model for AI Systems
note: The reference paper for everything else in this corpus. Introduces the tile abstraction, the three-level programming interface (beginner / developer / expert), layout inference, and the "composable" claim: high-level tile ops coexist with thread primitives in one kernel, lowered through TVM TIR.

title: TVM: An Automated End-to-End Optimizing Compiler for Deep Learning
note: The compiler TileLang is implemented on top of. Reading it explains the schedule/compute separation, the Halide-derived IR, and why TileLang can reuse TVM's lowering and target machinery instead of writing its own.

title: TensorIR: An Abstraction for Automatic Tensorized Program Optimization
note: Defines the block/axis IR that TileLang emits into. Inductor, TVM 0.9+ and TileLang all speak this dialect, so it is the vocabulary in which TileLang passes (layout inference, pipeline transform, warp specialization) are written.

title: Ansor: Generating High-Performance Tensor Programs for Deep Learning
note: The search-based auto-scheduling line of TVM. TileLang's autotuner inherits its split/reorder/fuse vocabulary, so this is the right background for understanding what TileLang deliberately does *not* do (it keeps the user in control of the tiling decision).

title: Tensor Program Optimization with Probabilistic Programs
note: The design behind TVM's MetaSchedule, which TileLang's autotuner sits on. Explains trace-based scheduling and the cost-model/search machinery that TileLang reuses for `autotune` runs on real hardware.

title: MLIR: A Compiler Infrastructure for the End of Moore's Law
note: The multi-level IR philosophy. TileLang keeps its own TVM/TIR path but the Ascend backend has an MLIR-based sibling (tilelang-mlir-ascend), so this is the common language between the two approaches.

title: The Deep Learning Compiler: A Comprehensive Survey
note: Best single orientation to the whole compiler landscape (graph IR, operator level, multi-level IR, backends). Use it as the first reading for anyone who has only used PyTorch and never seen a compiler pass pipeline.

title: Tensor Comprehensions: Framework-Agnostic High-Performance Machine Learning Abstractions
note: The polyhedral-scheduling ancestor of today's tensor DSLs. Shows the alternative design point (automatic scheduling) that TileLang consciously trades away for predictability and controllability.

title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
note: The canonical tile-based fusion argument: the roofline/IO analysis that gives TileLang's attention examples their reason to exist.

title: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning
note: Where the block partitioning, warp partitioning and shared-memory layout choices in TileLang's flash attention examples come from.

title: FlashAttention-3: Fast and Accurate Attention with Asynchrony and Low-precision
note: The Hopper-specific design (ping-pong warp specialization, async TMA/MMA) that TileLang's Hopper examples and its warp-specialization pass target.

title: T-MAC: CPU Renaissance via Table Lookup for Low-Bit LLM Deployment on Edge
note: Same MSRA group that produced BitBLAS and drove TileLang's early low-precision kernels. Useful for the origin story: TileLang grew out of a line of work on low-bit operator generation, not out of general-purpose compiler research.

title: TileSight: A First-Principles Tile-Centric Analytical GPU Performance Model from Cores to Clusters
note: Tile-centric analytical model; the companion repo lives in the same tile-ai org. Use it when reasoning about *why* a tiling choice wins, instead of guess-and-measure tuning.

title: Correct but Slow: An Empirical Study of the GPU Kernel Evaluation Gap in Modern Domain-Specific Languages
note: Empirical study of how DSL-generated kernels get evaluated in practice, including TileLang. Useful counterweight for the performance claims in vendor material.

title: AKG kernel Agent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Cross-Platform Kernel Synthesis
note: Agentic kernel synthesis across platforms, i.e. the "LLM writes the TileLang" direction. Relevant because TileLang ships an agent-oriented toolchain (see tilelang/tools and the [Ascend] agent PRs in the main repo).

title: StreamIndex: Memory-Bounded Compressed Sparse Attention via Streaming Top-k
note: Sparse-attention kernel work in the DeepSeek/DSA lineage that is implemented with TileLang-style tile kernels; shows what "frontier operator" means here.

title: MISA: Mixture of Indexer Sparse Attention for Long-Context LLM Inference
note: Sibling work to StreamIndex; documents the indexer/sparse-attention operator family that TileLang kernels target in 2026.

title: SeerAttention-R: Sparse Attention Adaptation for Long Reasoning
note: Reports its kernels as implemented in TileLang, including what had to be hand-written at the thread level. A concrete example of TileLang as the implementation vehicle for a research result.

title: Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention
note: DeepSeek's sparse-attention design; the operator family whose TileLang implementations (deepseek_nsa / dsa_* examples) are among the most demanding in-tree workloads.

title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
note: Defines MLA and the MoE structure that TileLang's flagship examples (deepseek_mla, fusedmoe, deepgemm) implement.

title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
note: Context for why DeepSeek's kernels (and hence TileLang's DeepSeek examples) became an industry reference point; kept for the workload-level narrative.

title: Pangu Ultra MoE: How to Train Your Big MoE on Ascend NPUs
note: Huawei's own account of training a large MoE on Ascend, including the software-stack constraints. Vendor source, and the least bad description of how the Ascend stack behaves at scale.

title: NPUEval: Optimizing NPU Kernels with LLMs and Open Source Compilers
note: Benchmark/eval for NPU kernel generation on Ascend; a concrete yardstick for the "LLM writes Ascend kernels" workflows that TileLang@Ascend is part of.

title: CUDA C++ Programming Guide
note: The grid/block/warp/thread model, the memory hierarchy, and the async primitives (cp.async, TMA, mbarrier). Everything TileLang's "expert level" interface exposes is defined here first.

title: CUDA C++ Best Practices Guide
note: Practical performance model: occupancy, coalescing, arithmetic intensity. The baseline against which kernel authors judge a tile configuration.

title: Parallel Thread Execution ISA
note: The instruction set TileLang ultimately emits. Read the sections on `mma`/`wgmma`/`tcgen05.mma`, `cp.async.bulk.tensor` (TMA), and the memory consistency model when you want to know what a TileLang intrinsic expands to.

title: Hopper Tuning Guide
note: Vendor tuning advice for sm90: TMA, clusters, distributed shared memory. The direct target of TileLang's cluster/TMA programming guide.

title: Blackwell Tuning Guide
note: sm100/sm120 specifics: tensor memory (TMEM), tcgen05 MMA, block scaling. TileLang already has tcgen05 examples and macro generators; this is the document that explains the constraints they encode.

title: CUTLASS Documentation
note: The C++ tile library TileLang competes with and partly mirrors (CuTe layouts, MMA atoms, epilogues). Reading it makes `T.gemm`'s layout/policy parameters much less magical.

title: CuTe: C++ template abstractions for layout algebra
note: Layout algebra (shape/stride/layout composition, tiling and partitioning of threads and values). TileLang's layout inference solves the same problem symbolically; this is the concrete formulation to compare against.

title: NVIDIA Hopper Architecture In-Depth
note: The vendor overview of Hopper: TMA (descriptor-based bulk async copy), thread block clusters and distributed shared memory, and the fourth-gen tensor core. This is the hardware story behind the `T.copy` -> TMA lowering and the cluster/TMA programming guide.

title: CUDA Blackwell Compatibility Guide
note: What changed for programs on Blackwell (sm100/sm120): new tensor-core and tensor-memory (TMEM) semantics, tcgen05 instructions, and the compatibility rules. Pair with the Blackwell Tuning Guide; the earlier blog-style architecture overview we tried to cite 404s, so this official guide is used instead.

title: Nsight Compute Documentation
note: How to measure a kernel: SOL sections, memory workload analysis, warp stalls. Needed for any serious tuning claim about a TileLang kernel.

title: Benchmarking and Dissecting the Nvidia Hopper GPU Architecture
note: Measured latencies/bandwidths for Hopper rather than vendor claims. The numbers you want when sanity-checking a pipeline stage count.

title: Dissecting the NVIDIA Volta GPU Architecture via Microbenchmarking
note: The original methodology paper for the Hopper/Blackwell dissections; useful when you need to measure an unfamiliar machine yourself.

title: Dissecting the NVidia Turing T4 GPU via Microbenchmarking
note: The intermediate step of the same series; retained for completeness of the hardware-model reading path.

title: NVIDIA/cuda-samples
note: Reference CUDA implementations (including Hopper TMA/WGMMA samples). When a TileLang codegen path looks odd, compare the generated CUDA against the vendor's own sample.

title: NVIDIA/cutlass
note: Source for the C++ tile abstractions TileLang's CuTe/PTX intrinsics mirror, including the tcgen05 and block-scaled MMA generators.

title: GPU MODE lectures
note: Community lecture series on GPU programming that repeatedly covers TileLang alongside CUDA/Triton. Good source of talk recordings and slides links for the learning-path document.

title: CANN 异构计算架构总览
note: Entry point to CANN: GE/Graph Engine, runtime, compiler (bisheng), operator libraries, HCCL. Establishes which layer a given Ascend problem belongs to.

title: Ascend C 算子开发
note: The C/C++ kernel language TileLang@Ascend's PTO route lowers to. Reading it first makes the comparison "what does TileLang remove from Ascend C" concrete.

title: CANN 编译器（毕昇编译器）
note: Huawei's LLVM-based compiler for Host-Device heterogeneous code. The backend TileLang's generated source is handed to.

title: 昇腾算子开发场景
note: Vendor overview of the operator development options available on Ascend (Ascend C, TBE, Triton, and now TileLang), useful for positioning TileLang inside Huawei's own story.

title: TileLang AscendNPU IR 从入门到专家算子开发知识点
note: Huawei's own TileLang+Ascend training material: TileLang and MLIR basics, Pythonic programming, and a hand-written FlashAttention operator. The most direct official bridge between the two halves of this corpus.

title: CANN 开源项目列表
note: Map of Huawei's open-sourced CANN components (Ascend C, CATLASS, PTO, graph engine, ...). Use it as the authoritative list of where the source lives.

title: cann/pto-isa — PTO instruction set architecture
note: The PTO (Programmable Tensor Operations) ISA specification — the tile-level instruction set that TileLang@Ascend's PTO backend targets, and the subject of the 知乎 author's article series.

title: cann/catlass — Ascend C template library
note: Huawei's CUTLASS analogue for Ascend C. The baseline TileLang@Ascend GEMM kernels are benchmarked against.

title: huawei-csl/pto-dsl
note: A Pythonic interface and JIT compiler for PTO-ISA — i.e. Huawei's own tile-DSL experiment next to TileLang. Comparing the two designs is one of the more informative exercises in this corpus.

title: PTO-ISA/pto-spec
note: Formal definition of the PTO ISA (normative language / ASL model). The precise semantics behind the Ascend tile instruction set.

title: PTO-ISA/PTO-Gym
note: Tile-operation tutorials and examples for PTO-based programming; the hands-on half of the PTO spec.

title: huawei-csl/pto-kernels
note: Hand-written PTO kernels. These are the performance ceiling that a TileLang kernel on Ascend has to be compared against.

title: huawei-csl/megagdn-pto
note: Megakernel for Gated DeltaNet written with PTO-ISA. A concrete "what the low-level tile ISA can express" example on Ascend.

title: PTO-ISA/pyCircuit
note: Python-first hardware construction toolkit with MLIR compilation. Included because the 知乎 author's article set treats it as the hardware-generation end of the same PTO story, and it shows where the tile abstraction is heading beyond kernel writing.

title: tile-ai/tilelang-ascend
note: The dedicated Ascend adapter: two backend routes (Ascend C & PTO, and AscendNPU IR), a programming guide, per-operator tutorials, and DeepSeek V4 kernels. This is the single most important source for the Huawei side.

title: tile-ai/tilelang-mlir-ascend
note: The MLIR-based Ascend path. Where the TVM/TIR route and the MLIR route diverge is exactly the kind of question a would-be backend contributor has to answer, so both sources are needed.

title: tile-ai/TileFoundry
note: Infrastructure for standing up new TileLang backends. Read together with 08-frontier-unmerged/raw/github-issue-2115 (multi-backend refactoring) to understand how a third chip vendor is expected to plug in.

title: [RoadMap] Multi-Backend Refactoring/Decoupling
note: The roadmap that made the Ascend/Hygon/MUSA adapters possible: how TileLang intends to decouple new backends from the CUDA-centric core. Essential for anyone planning to contribute a backend.

title: RFC: migrate tilelang from TileLang/tvm to apache/tvm + apache/tvm-ffi
note: An open RFC with large blast radius: leaving the forked TVM for upstream TVM plus tvm-ffi. Explains a lot of in-flight churn in the tree.

title: [RFC] Add explicit CUDA cache policies for normal global-memory copies
note: Representative of the fine-grained control RFCs: exposing cache hints on plain global copies. Shows the level at which TileLang contributors argue.

title: [RFC] Redesign reducers as ownership-safe deferred reductions
note: Semantics-level RFC on reductions and buffer ownership; the kind of problem you meet as soon as you try to add a new reduction op or a new backend.

title: [RFC] Define memory-order behavior for legacy CUDA atomic-add fallbacks
note: Memory-order semantics of atomics across codegen paths — a good test case for whether you actually understand TileLang's lowering.

title: [Roadmap] Release Plan of tilelang 0.2.0
note: The 0.2.0 plan; useful for dating features and for seeing which pieces were considered core versus experimental at that point.

title: [Roadmap] Roadmap for Metal, OpenCL, VHLS, WebGPU, and SPIR-V Support
note: The non-NVIDIA backend roadmap (Metal/WebGPU/SPIR-V). Read it for the pattern a new target follows, even though this corpus ignores those chips.

title: [RoadMap] CuteDSL Backend
note: The CuTe DSL backend line. It matters because it defines the boundary between TileLang's own lowering and NVIDIA's newer Python tile DSL (cuTile/CuTe DSL), which is the most serious competitor on the NVIDIA side.

title: [Public Release 9/30] Introduce Ascend 950 backend
note: The PR that brought the Ascend 950 backend into mainline TileLang. The diff and review discussion are the most direct description of the Ascend/codegen surface that exists.

title: [Ascend] Add PTO backend for Ascend950
note: Adds the PTO codegen target for Ascend 950 — the second of the two Ascend backend routes, and the one that connects to PTO-ISA/pyPTO.

title: [Ascend] Add T.PersistentKernel and AutoPersistent pass
note: In-flight Ascend feature: persistent kernels plus the pass that derives them. An example of frontier work that has not landed, exactly what the user asked to keep an eye on.

title: feat(ascend): Add AutoSimtVF pass and register it in Ascend pipeline
note: In-flight: automatic SIMT/vector-fragment lowering for Ascend. Shows how the "tile -> SIMD/SIMT region" boundary is still being negotiated.

title: [Ascend] Add TileLang agents for operator generation and tuning
note: In-flight: LLM agents that write and tune Ascend TileLang operators. Signals where the project expects operator development to go next.

title: [Question] It seems there are two Ascend 950 backends, which is suggested to use
note: The maintainer discussion of Ascend C&PTO versus AscendNPU IR. Tl;dr-level guidance for choosing a route, straight from the people who wrote both.

title: DeepSeek 开源昇腾基础组件将会带来哪些影响？
tags: tilelang, ascend, ascend-950, z3, layout, sync
note: The single 知乎 article the user pointed at, and the best Chinese-language account of TileLang's Ascend port. Covers the NV-vs-950 architectural mismatch table, the new Ascend-specific intrinsics (T.alloc_l1/l0a/l0b/l0c, T.SimtVF/T.SimdVF, T.dual_copy), layout inference and ND->NZ fractal normalization, and how Z3 is used to solve the multi-pipeline scheduling and buffer-multiplicity constraints that Ascend C leaves to the human. Full text and images live in 09-zhihu-da-zhi-ruo-yu/raw/answers/.

title: TileLang-Ascend 视频课程（5 讲）
note: Official course: environment setup, programming basics, the developer programming model, performance-tuning/debug tools, and deployment. Recorded in Chinese; the companion repo is tile-ai/tilelang-ascend. (Only the landing page is archived here; this corpus does not mirror video.)

title: tile-ai/tilelang-puzzles
note: Ten graded exercises that teach TileLang by making you write kernels. The best existing starting point for the "learn by doing" track of a course.

title: tile-ai/TileOPs
note: High-performance LLM operator library built on TileLang. The natural reference for "what production TileLang kernels look like", including integration with PyTorch/vLLM.

title: tile-ai/TileRT
note: Tile-based runtime for ultra-low-latency LLM inference. Shows what the kernels are deployed into, and the launch/scheduling constraints that come back as compiler requirements.

title: tile-ai/tilelang-benchmark
note: The project's own benchmark harness. Needed if you intend to make performance claims or detect regressions in a contribution.

title: tile-ai/tilelang-lsp
note: Language server for TileLang kernels. Minor for learning, but it documents the developer-experience side of the frontend.

title: Triton: An Intermediate Language and Compiler for Tiled Neural Network Computations
note: The original Triton paper (DOI 10.1145/3315508.3329973), mirrored locally as triton-mapl-2019.pdf with a page-by-page text extraction in triton-mapl-2019.md. This is the design point TileLang is measured against: Triton treats the program as blocks over a tensor with a compiler-chosen schedule; TileLang keeps explicit tiles, layouts and memory placement in the language. Read it for what "tiled intermediate language" originally meant, and note that the 2019 language is much smaller than today's Triton.

title: triton-lang/triton
note: The Triton implementation, i.e. TileLang's most common comparison target. The original paper is "Triton: An Intermediate Language and Compiler for Tiled Neural Network Computations" (MAPL 2019, DOI 10.1145/3315508.3329973); it is not mirrored here because the open copies we probed 404 and the ACM PDF is bot-blocked, so cite the DOI and use this repo plus the docs for detail. The decisive contrast with TileLang is that Triton hides the tile and lets the compiler pick the schedule, while TileLang keeps explicit tiles, layouts and memory placement in the language.

title: Triton documentation
note: Current Triton language/API reference, for side-by-side reading with the TileLang language guide.

title: CuTe DSL 文档（CUTLASS Python DSL）
note: NVIDIA 官方的 Python tile DSL 文档。它是 TileLang 在 NVIDIA 侧最直接的对照物： 同样用 Python 写 tile 程序，但绑定 CUTLASS/CuTe 的抽象与 NVIDIA 自己的编译路径。 第 5 章对比与第 24 章 NVIDIA 后端都用它来界定「TileLang 自己的边界在哪里」。

title: NVIDIA/cutile-python
note: cuTile 的开源实现（Python 包）。NVIDIA 新一代 tile 编程模型，面向 Blackwell 一代的硬件特性；与 TileLang 属于同一抽象层次的竞争路线。第 1、5、24 章引用它 说明「tile DSL」这一波的产业走向。

title: Apache TVM documentation
note: Upstream TVM/TIR documentation: IR structure, schedules, target/device abstraction. TileLang is a TVM dialect in practice, so this is its standard library documentation.

title: MLIR documentation
note: Dialect and pass infrastructure. Required reading for the AscendNPU IR route, which is MLIR-based rather than TVM-based.

title: Halide documentation — a language for fast, portable data-parallel computation
note: The ancestor of the "separate algorithm from schedule" idea that TVM adopted and TileLang re-specialised for AI tiles.

title: torch.compile documentation
note: The graph-capture/Inductor pipeline that a TileLang kernel has to fit into when it is used from PyTorch. Explains the boundary TileLang does *not* cover (graph-level fusion and autotuning).

title: PyTorch Inductor: generated kernels
note: How to see the kernels Inductor generates. The practical way to decide when torch.compile is enough and when a TileLang kernel has to be dropped in.

title: Hugging Face Transformers 文档
note: 端到端章节的基础工具文档：模型加载、tokenizer、Trainer/训练参数、混合精度、 checkpoint 保存与恢复。第 17 章「用 HF 资产训练 7B」直接依赖它。 （原地址 https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/index 在本机不可达：huggingface.co 直连与走本地代理均 SSL EOF，改用中国镜像 hf-mirror.com 抓取；镜像内容与官网一致，引用时以原地址为准。）

title: deepseek-ai/DeepEP（NVIDIA 版）

title: deepseek-ai/FlashMLA

title: Ascend Sparse Attention Forward 算法与优化技术简析

title: deepseek-ai/DeepSelect

title: DeepSelect 算法与实现简析
note: 含随机块序下的期望复杂度证明，以及 CUDA 侧用 PTX 与位运算压低常数的技巧。

title: deepseek-ai/DeepJIT
note: DeepGEMM-Ascend 与 DeepEP-Ascend 共用的运行时编译层。 和 TileLang 自己的 JIT 是同一层抽象的两个实现，值得对照。

title: deepseek-ai/Engram：Conditional Memory via Scalable Lookup
note: TileKernels 里 Engram 算子的来源论文与参考实现。仓库内含 Engram_paper.pdf。

title: Conditional Memory via Scalable Lookup: A New Axis of Sparsity for LLMs（Engram 论文）
note: TileKernels 里 Engram 算子族的来源论文。给出 MoE（条件计算）与 Engram（条件记忆） 之间的容量分配 scaling law，并说明为什么确定性寻址可以把大表卸载到 host memory。 本地文本抽取见 14-deepseek-ascend-stack/raw/paper-deepseek-engram.md。

title: mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections
note: TileKernels 的 mhc/ 算子族与 DeepGEMM-Ascend 的 HC prenorm GEMM 的论文依据。 第 4.3 节（Kernel Fusion / Recomputing / Overlapping Communication in DualPipe） 正是这几个 kernel 与 DualPipe 的设计来源。本地文本抽取见 14-deepseek-ascend-stack/raw/paper-deepseek-mhc.md，PDF 为 paper-deepseek-mhc.pdf。

title: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp
